concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: Asymptotic upper bound on growth.

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Sums of coefficients times powers of a variable.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a+bi with roots of unity.

concepts.name: Multitape Turing machine
concepts.gloss: A deterministic machine with finite alphabet and a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes; time is the number of steps.

concepts.name: Schönhage–Strassen n log n conjecture and history
concepts.gloss: Schönhage and Strassen multiplied n-bit integers in O(n log n log log n) on a multitape machine and conjectured n log n optimal; Harvey–van der Hoeven reached O(n log n).

evidence.quote:
Sch\"onhage and Strassen proved in 1971 that two $n$-bit integers can
be multiplied in $O(n\log n\log\log n)$ time on a multitape Turing
machine

concepts.name: Convolution and the discrete Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: Convolution of coefficient lists is computed by transforming, multiplying pointwise, and transforming back using roots of unity.

evidence.quote:
Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to
convolution of short integer coefficients.

concepts.name: Multiplication as digit convolution
concepts.gloss: Splitting the inputs into radix digits turns integer multiplication into convolution of short integer coefficients, followed by carry propagation.

evidence.quote:
Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to
convolution of short integer coefficients.

concepts.name: Signed coefficient packing (Kronecker substitution)
concepts.gloss: Packing polynomial coefficients into one long integer so a polynomial product becomes an integer product.

evidence.quote:
Signed coefficient
packing is a form of Kronecker substitution

concepts.name: Established O(n log n) multiplier as subroutine
concepts.gloss: The Harvey–van der Hoeven O(n log n) algorithm, called as an ordinary subroutine for small polynomial products without recursively invoking the new theorem.

evidence.quote:
Calls to the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier are ordinary subroutine
calls

concepts.name: Elementary stream operations on tapes
concepts.gloss: Array order, scans, controlled shifts and rational scalings that a fixed-tape machine performs in linear time.

evidence.quote: \section{The machine model and elementary streams}

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1
concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r + 1$

symbols.name: ring variable
symbols.meaning: The indeterminate of the polynomials, with y^r = -1.

symbols.name: number of coefficients
symbols.meaning: The number of coefficients in a polynomial, a power of two.

concepts.gloss: Polynomials in y with complex coefficients reduced using y^r = −1; powers of y act as roots of unity and multiplying by one is a signed cyclic shift of the coefficient list.

evidence.quote: one coordinate is stored as the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$, with $r$ a power of two

multiplication by
such a root is a signed shift of the coefficient list

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transforms
concepts.gloss: Fourier-type transforms over the polynomial ring where powers of y serve as roots of unity, built from address rearrangements, signed shifts and two-point butterflies (Nussbaumer).

evidence.quote:
These are the
synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle and
Nussbaumer

the transform calculation consists of address
rearrangements, signed shifts, and two-point butterfly operations

concepts.name: Exact normalized polynomial products
concepts.gloss: Convolution over the ring using the forward synthetic transforms, pointwise polynomial products via signed packing and the O(n log n) multiplier, and the opposite transform.

evidence.quote:
The two forward synthetic transforms
retain the same frequency order through their pointwise product

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder map to prime cyclic axes
concepts.gloss: Placing the coefficient list on a product of distinct prime cyclic axes by a Chinese-remainder map that preserves convolution.

evidence.quote:
the radix-digit coefficient list is placed on a
product of distinct prime cyclic axes by a Chinese-remainder map that preserves
convolution

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: Harvey–van der Hoeven identity expressing a Fourier transform on prime-length axes through a multidimensional transform with power-of-two axis lengths; the coordinate permutations are retained in the identity.

evidence.quote:
Gaussian
resampling then expresses each source Fourier transform through a
power-of-two tensor transform

retains the
source and target coordinate permutations in the transform identity

concepts.name: Bluestein chirp identity
concepts.gloss: Converts a Fourier transform (with its target permutation) into a cyclic convolution via multiplication by chirp phases.

evidence.quote:
Bluestein's chirp identity converts the middle transform,
including its target permutation, into normalized cyclic convolution.

concepts.name: Last-coordinate phase twist
concepts.gloss: A phase twist turning the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial modulo y^r+1, whose negative wrap yields the original cyclic wrap once the twist is removed.

evidence.quote:
A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial
modulo $y^r+1$

concepts.name: Linear networks, roles and frames
concepts.gloss: A fixed linear network exchanging two banks of values with signs and restoring auxiliary values; roles are wire positions and invertible frames D_v change the stored representation so intermediate frames cancel and only an endpoint operator remains.

evidence.quote:
Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two
banks of values, with prescribed signs, and restores every auxiliary
value.
We call $D_v$ its frame

concepts.name: Finite network from three-element subsets
concepts.gloss: Subspaces of a fixed m-dimensional space attached to gates, built from three-element subsets with gather/scatter and auxiliary wires, giving a total number of smaller calls s less than W·m.

evidence.quote:
The construction uses
three-element subsets: gather and scatter create coefficients depending
on intersection size, and auxiliary wires cancel the unwanted
coefficients.

The decisive property is that the total
number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$.

concepts.name: Recursive power saving s < Wm
concepts.title: Recursive power saving from $s<Wm$

symbols.name: number of smaller calls
symbols.meaning: The total number of smaller calls the network makes.

symbols.name: number of roles
symbols.meaning: The number of roles (wires) in the network, among which rows are distributed.

symbols.name: parameter multiplier
symbols.meaning: The dimension of the fixed space and factor by which the recursive parameter grows per level.

concepts.gloss: Recursing at parameter m·f uses s calls at parameter f on volume V/W each; since s/W < m the volume-normalized cost grows by less than a factor m per level, giving a power of the parameter below the first power.

evidence.quote:
This strict inequality
is the source of the power saving.

concepts.name: Restoring auxiliary values
concepts.gloss: Scratch registers with arbitrary initial contents are subtracted, used, re-added and the computation reversed so the final effect is exact for any initial auxiliary values.

evidence.quote:
The final permutation is
exact for arbitrary initial auxiliary values.

concepts.name: Address shear and triangular factorization
concepts.gloss: Fields updated by (H,D) -> (H+D,D) over a residue ring; rational matrix shears are factored into lower-triangular pieces (Bruhat factorization) so they can be implemented cheaply in tape order.

evidence.quote: that endpoint operator is an address shear
Lower triangular factorization

concepts.name: Fast interchange of address fields
concepts.title: Fast interchange of address fields: cost $Vu^\tau$

symbols.name: stored bit volume
symbols.meaning: The number of bits stored in the array.

symbols.name: field width
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each interchanged address field.

symbols.name: exponent
symbols.meaning: A fixed constant strictly less than 1.

concepts.gloss: Exchanging two disjoint contiguous u-bit address fields of an array with volume V in O(V u^τ) time for fixed τ<1, using XOR combinations of intermediate data though the final effect is an exact permutation.

evidence.quote:
The first procedure interchanges two disjoint contiguous address fields
of $u$ bits in an array whose addresses form a complete Cartesian
product.

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer H₀
concepts.title: Simultaneous butterfly layer $H_0(u,v)$

symbols.name: first value
symbols.meaning: The first input value of the two-point butterfly.

symbols.name: second value
symbols.meaning: The second input value of the two-point butterfly.

concepts.gloss: Applying H_0(u,v)=((u+v)/2,(u−v)/2) coefficientwise on selected address bits of numerical arrays of complex fixed-point polynomial records, via the recursive network, in O(V d^λ') time.

evidence.quote: simultaneously on selected coordinate bits of the numerical arrays
Intermediate values are exact Gaussian dyadics

concepts.name: Fixed-point precision and exact recovery
concepts.gloss: Gaussian dyadic intermediates with a single truncation after a contractive layer; the recovered coefficient error is kept below 1/2 so rounding and carries give the exact integer product.

evidence.quote:
A single
truncation follows the completed contractive layer.

proves that the recovered
coefficient error is strictly below $1/2$

concepts.name: Transform layout with retained frequency order and permutations
concepts.gloss: Tape layout on which the parallel layers apply; permutations from resampling and chirps are kept inside the transform and cancel across forward, pointwise product and opposite transforms rather than being sorted.

evidence.quote:
the source permutation retained during resampling cancels
across the two forward source transforms

concepts.name: Multiplication algorithm and its cost
concepts.gloss: Chain the reductions: digits, prime axes, Gaussian resampling and chirps, phase twist, ring convolution with fast interchanges and butterfly layers, then rescaling, rounding and carries; the cost table fits n(lg n)^(1−κ).

evidence.quote:
A compatible choice of rational
parameters makes all terms in its cost table fit Theorem

concepts.name: Integer multiplication below n log n
concepts.title: Integer multiplication in time $n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa}$

symbols.name: input length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two integers being multiplied.

symbols.name: power saving
symbols.meaning: The fixed constant 2^{-182} giving the saving in the logarithmic factor.

concepts.gloss: A fixed deterministic multitape Turing machine multiplies two n-bit integers in O(n (lg n)^(1−κ)) worst-case time with κ = 2^−182, refuting the n log n optimality conjecture in this model.

evidence.quote:
We give a deterministic algorithm that multiplies two $n$-bit integers
in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ worst-case time

concepts.name: Binary representation of integers
concepts.gloss: A nonnegative integer is written as a string of bits with place values powers of two, padded with leading zeros to a fixed length.

concepts.name: Logarithms and ceiling/floor
concepts.gloss: lg n is the base-2 logarithm, and ceiling and floor round a real number up or down to an integer.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic on integers where numbers differing by a multiple of m are identified, with addition and multiplication well defined on residues.

concepts.name: Prime numbers and coprimality
concepts.gloss: A prime has no divisors besides 1 and itself, and integers are coprime when their greatest common divisor is 1.

concepts.name: Bitwise XOR
concepts.gloss: The bit operation giving 1 exactly when its two inputs differ, equal to addition modulo 2, and self-inverse.

concepts.name: Matrices and linear maps
concepts.gloss: Linear maps between vector spaces are represented by matrices, composed by matrix multiplication, invertible when an inverse exists, and triangular when entries above or below the diagonal vanish.

concepts.name: Vector subspaces and dimension
concepts.gloss: A subspace is a set of vectors closed under addition and scaling, with dimension equal to the size of any basis.

concepts.name: Cartesian product and index sets
concepts.gloss: The set of tuples with each coordinate from its own set, used to index multidimensional arrays.

concepts.name: Permutations
concepts.gloss: A permutation is a bijective rearrangement of a finite set of positions.

concepts.name: Fixed-point and rounding
concepts.gloss: Real numbers are stored as integers scaled by a power of two, and rounding or truncation discards low-order digits, introducing a bounded error.

concepts.name: Absolute value, modulus and sup norm
concepts.gloss: Size measures for numbers and vectors, with the sup norm the largest absolute entry, obeying the triangle inequality.

concepts.name: Schoolbook multiplication and carries
concepts.gloss: The grade-school method of multiplying numbers digit by digit and propagating carries, taking quadratic time.

concepts.name: Divide and conquer recursion
concepts.gloss: Solving a problem by recursive calls on smaller instances and combining results, with running time analysed by a recurrence.

concepts.name: Induction and proof by contradiction
concepts.gloss: Standard proof techniques used throughout discrete mathematics.

concepts.name: Linear-time scanning of tape data
concepts.gloss: A Turing machine head can read, copy or transform an n-cell tape contents in time proportional to n by sweeping across it.

concepts.name: Euclidean division and floor division
concepts.gloss: Every integer a and positive m give a unique quotient q and remainder r with a = qm + r and 0 <= r < m.

concepts.name: Geometric series and exponent rules
concepts.gloss: Sums of the form 1 + r + r^2 + ... have closed forms, and powers obey the usual exponent laws.

background.summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science background: asymptotic analysis, discrete mathematics (binary numbers, modular arithmetic, primes, XOR, subsets), introductory linear algebra (matrices, invertibility, vector subspaces, dimension), and basic complex numbers and polynomials. They know basic Turing machines with tapes, and have seen the standard FFT idea at most as an algorithm, not the Nussbaumer, Bluestein or Harvey-van der Hoeven machinery. They have not studied algebraic number theory, advanced algebra such as Bruhat factorization, or numerical error analysis in depth.
